title: From Parametric Sines and Cosines to an Ellipse Equation
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph x = 3 cos t, y = 2 sin t over one full period. Find the Cartesian equation of the curve, name its semi-axes, and comment on how the plot compares with the unit circle parametrization.

steps.title: Isolate the trig functions and eliminate t
steps.explanation: Dividing each coordinate by its amplitude and squaring produces the standard ellipse equation centered at the origin.
steps.why: Every parametrization of the form (a cos t, b sin t) collapses to the same identity, so the elimination is exact rather than an approximation read off the screen.

steps.title: Read off the geometry
steps.explanation: The horizontal semi-axis is 3 and the vertical semi-axis is 2, so the curve is the unit circle stretched by 3 horizontally and 2 vertically.
steps.why: Amplitudes in a parametrization act as scale factors, which is exactly the shifting-and-scaling idea applied to parametric plots.

steps.title: Choose a window that preserves the shape
steps.explanation: The window clears both intercept sets with a small margin, and with a locked 1:1 scale the ellipse looks correctly flattened rather than circular or stretched.
steps.why: Unequal axis scaling can make an ellipse of axes 3 and 2 appear nearly round, misleading the reader about the actual ratio.
